rule.returned: active again on a later day, within 14 days of their own first day

caveats: GA4 counts browsers, not people. It knows a reader by a cookie: one person on a phone and a computer is two readers, and a cleared cookie or a new browser makes a returning reader look new.

Safari and some other browsers expire a cookie set by a script after about 7 days without a visit, so a reader who comes back after a week can be counted as new. That pushes the return share DOWN, not up.
Readers who send Global Privacy Control, who turned analytics off on /privacy, who block Google Analytics, or whose browser is automated are not counted at all, on any day.
US only, with the same server towns removed as every other GA4 figure in this file. A reader who was in a server town, or outside the US, on their first day is not in a cohort.
GA4 sends no row for a day with no returns; such a day counts as zero returns.
These are estimates for watching a trend, not exact counts.
